On closed rational functions in several variables

A. P. Petravchuk Note: Kiev Taras Shevchenko University, Faculty of Mechanics and Mathematics, 64, Volodymyrska street, 01033 Kyiv, Ukraine, e-mail: aptr@univ.kiev.ua    O. G. Iena Note:  Kiev Taras Shevchenko University and Technische Universität Kaiserslautern, Fachbereich Mathematik, Postfach 3049, 67653 Kaiserslautern, Germany, e-mail: yena@mathematik.uni-kl.de
Abstract

Let 𝕂=𝕂¯\mathbb{K}=\bar{\mathbb{K}} be a field of characteristic zero. An element φ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\varphi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) is called a closed rational function if the subfield 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is algebraically closed in the field 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}). We prove that a rational function φ=f/g\varphi=f/g is closed if ff and gg are algebraically independent and at least one of them is irreducible. We also show that the rational function φ=f/g\varphi=f/g is closed if and only if the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g contains only finitely many reducible hypersurfaces. Some sufficient conditions for a polynomial to be irreducible are given.

1 Introduction

Closed polynomials, i. e., polynomials f∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]f\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] such that the subalgebra 𝕂⁡[f]\mathbb{K}[f] is integrally closed in 𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}], were studied by many authors (see, for example, [Now], [Stein], [Najib],[Arzh] ). A rational analogue of a closed polynomial is a rational function φ\varphi such that the subfield 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is algebraically closed in the field 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}), such a rational function will be called a closed one. Although there are algorithms to determine whether a given rational function is closed (see [Oll]) it is interesting to study closed rational functions more detailed.

We give the following sufficient condition for a rational function to be closed. Let φ=f/g∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\varphi=f/g\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}), ff and gg are coprime, algebraically independent and at least one of polynomials ff and gg is irreducible. Then φ\varphi is a closed rational function (Theorem 1).

Using some results of of J.M. Ollagnier [Oll] about Darboux polynomials we prove that a rational function φ=f/g∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi=f/g\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} is closed if and only if the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g of hypersurfaces contains only finitely many reducible hypersurfaces (Theorem 2). We also study products of irreducible polynomials.

Notations in the paper are standard. For a rational function F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t) of the form F⁡(t)=P⁡(t)Q⁡(t)F(t)=\frac{P(t)}{Q(t)} with coprime polynomials PP and QQ the degree is deg⁡F=max⁡(deg⁡P,deg⁡Q)\deg F=\max(\deg P,\deg Q). The ground field 𝕂\mathbb{K} is algebraically closed of characteristic 00.

2 Closed rational functions in several variables

Lemma 1.

For a rational functions φ,ψ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi,\psi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} the following conditions are equivalent.

1) φ\varphi and ψ\psi are algebraically dependent over 𝕂\mathbb{K};

2) the rank of Jacobi matrix J⁡(φ,ψ)=(∂φ∂x1…∂φ∂xn∂ψ∂x1…∂ψ∂xn)J(\varphi,\psi)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x_{1}}&\dots&\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial x_{n}}\\ \frac{\partial\psi}{\partial x_{1}}&\dots&\frac{\partial\psi}{\partial x_{n}}\end{pmatrix} is equal to 11;

3) for differentials d​φd{\varphi} and d​ψd{\psi} of functions φ\varphi and ψ\psi respectively it holds d​φ∧d​ψ=0d{\varphi}\wedge d{\psi}=0;

4) there exists h∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)h\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) such that φ=F⁡(h)\varphi=F(h) and ψ=G⁡(h)\psi=G(h) for some F⁡(t),G⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t),G(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t).

Proof.

The equivalence of 1) and 2) follows from [Hodge], Ch.III, §7, Th. III. The equivalence of 2) and 3) is obvious. Since 2) clearly follows from 4), it remains to show that 1) implies 4). Let φ\varphi and ψ\psi be algebraically dependent. Then obviously tr.deg𝕂⁡𝕂⁡(φ,ψ)=1\trdeg_{\mathbb{K}}\mathbb{K}(\varphi,\psi)=1. By Theorem of Gordan (see for example [Schinz], p.15) 𝕂⁡(φ,ψ)=𝕂⁡(h)\mathbb{K}(\varphi,\psi)=\mathbb{K}(h) for some rational function hh and therefore φ=F⁡(h)\varphi=F(h) and ψ=G⁡(h)\psi=G(h) for some F⁡(t),G⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t),G(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t). ∎

Definition 1.

We call a rational function φ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} closed if the subfield 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is algebraically closed in 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}).

A rational function ψ~\tilde{\psi} is called generative for a rational function ψ\psi if ψ~\tilde{\psi} is closed and ψ∈𝕂⁡(ψ~)\psi\in\mathbb{K}(\tilde{\psi}).

Lemma 2.

1) For a rational function φ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} the following conditions are equivalent.

a) φ\varphi is closed;

b) 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is a maximal element in the partially ordered (by inclusion) set of subfields of 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) of the form 𝕂⁡(ψ)\mathbb{K}(\psi), ψ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\psi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K}.

c) φ\varphi is non-composite rational function, i. e., from the equality φ=F⁡(ψ)\varphi=F(\psi), for some rational functions ψ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\psi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} and F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t), it follows that deg⁡F=1\deg F=1.

2) For every rational function φ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} there exists a generative rational function φ~\tilde{\varphi}. If φ~1\tilde{\varphi}_{1} and φ~2\tilde{\varphi}_{2} are two generative rational functions for φ\varphi, then φ~2=a​φ~1+bc​φ~1+d\tilde{\varphi}_{2}=\frac{a\tilde{\varphi}_{1}+b}{c\tilde{\varphi}_{1}+d} for some a,b,c,d∈𝕂a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{K} such that a​d−b​c≠0.ad-bc\not=0.

Proof.

1) a)⇒\Rightarrow b). Suppose that the rational function φ\varphi is closed and 𝕂⁡(φ)⊆𝕂⁡(ψ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi)\subseteq\mathbb{K}(\psi) for some ψ∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\psi\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}). The element ψ\psi is algebraic over over 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) and therefore by the definition of closed rational functions we have ψ∈𝕂⁡(φ)\psi\in\mathbb{K}(\varphi). Thus 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is a maximal element in the set of all one-generated subfields of 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}).

b)⇒\Rightarrow a). If 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is a maximal one-generated subfield of 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}), then 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is algebraically closed in 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}). Indeed, if ff is algebraic over 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi), then tr.deg𝕂⁡(φ,f)=1\trdeg_{\mathbb{K}}(\varphi,f)=1 and by Theorem of Gordan 𝕂⁡(φ,f)=𝕂⁡(ψ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi,f)=\mathbb{K}(\psi) for some rational function ψ\psi. But then 𝕂⁡(ψ)=𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\psi)=\mathbb{K}(\varphi) and f∈𝕂⁡(φ)f\in\mathbb{K}(\varphi).

The equivalence of b) and c) is obvious.

2) The subfield 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) is contained in some maximal one-generated subfield 𝕂⁡(φ~)\mathbb{K}(\tilde{\varphi}), which is algebraically closed in 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) by the part 1) of this Lemma. Therefore φ~\tilde{\varphi} is a generative rational function for φ\varphi.

Let φ~1\tilde{\varphi}_{1} and φ~2\tilde{\varphi}_{2} be two generative rational functions for φ\varphi. Then φ~1\tilde{\varphi}_{1} and φ~2\tilde{\varphi}_{2} are algebraic over the field 𝕂⁡(φ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi) and therefore tr.deg𝕂⁡𝕂⁡(φ,φ~1,φ~2)=1\trdeg_{\mathbb{K}}\mathbb{K}(\varphi,\tilde{\varphi}_{1},\tilde{\varphi}_{2})=1. In particular, then the rational functions φ~1\tilde{\varphi}_{1} and φ~2\tilde{\varphi}_{2} are algebraically dependent.

By Lemma 1 one obtains φ~1∈𝕂⁡(ψ)\tilde{\varphi}_{1}\in\mathbb{K}(\psi), φ~2∈𝕂⁡(ψ)\tilde{\varphi}_{2}\in\mathbb{K}(\psi) for some rational function ψ\psi. Since both φ~1\tilde{\varphi}_{1} and φ~2\tilde{\varphi}_{2} are closed, we get 𝕂⁡(φ~1)=𝕂⁡(ψ)=𝕂⁡(φ~2)\mathbb{K}(\tilde{\varphi}_{1})=\mathbb{K}(\psi)=\mathbb{K}(\tilde{\varphi}_{2}). But there exists a fractional rational transformation θ\theta of the field 𝕂⁡(ψ)\mathbb{K}(\psi) such that θ⁡(φ~2)=φ~1\theta(\tilde{\varphi}_{2})=\tilde{\varphi}_{1}. Therefore, φ~2=a​φ~1+bc​φ~1+d\tilde{\varphi}_{2}=\frac{a\tilde{\varphi}_{1}+b}{c\tilde{\varphi}_{1}+d}, for some a,b,c,d∈𝕂,a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{K}, a​d−b​c≠0ad-bc\neq 0. ∎

Remark 1.

Note that algebraically dependent rational functions have the same set of generative functions. This follows from Lemma 1 and Lemma 2.

Remark 2.

Let f∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]∖𝕂.f\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}]\setminus\mathbb{K}. By Lemma 3 from [Arzh], the subfield 𝕂⁡(f)\mathbb{K}(f) is algebraically closed if and only if the polynomial ff is closed. So, the polynomial ff is closed if and only if ff is closed as a rational function.

Theorem 1.

Let polynomials f,g∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]f,g\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] be coprime and algebraically independent. If at least one of them is irreducible, then the rational function φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} is closed.

Proof.

Without loss of generality we can assume that ff is irreducible. By Lemma 2 there exists a generative rational function ψ=pq\psi=\frac{p}{q} for φ\varphi, where pp and qq are coprime polynomials. Then φ=P⁡(ψ)Q⁡(ψ)\varphi=\frac{P(\psi)}{Q(\psi)} for some coprime polynomials P⁡(t),Q⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡[t]P(t),Q(t)\in\mathbb{K}[t].

Let P⁡(t)=a0​(t−λ1)​…​(t−λm)P(t)=a_{0}(t-\lambda_{1})\dots(t-\lambda_{m}) and Q⁡(t)=b0​(t−μ1)​…​(t−μl)Q(t)=b_{0}(t-\mu_{1})\dots(t-\mu_{l}), λi,μj∈𝕂\lambda_{i},\mu_{j}\in\mathbb{K} be the decompositions of P⁡(t)P(t) and Q⁡(t)Q(t) into irreducible factors. Then

φ=fg=a0​(pq−λ1)​…​(pq−λm)b0​(pq−μ1)​…​(pq−μl)=a0​(p−λ1​q)​…​(p−λm​q)​ql−mb0​(p−μ1​q)​…​(p−μl​q).\varphi=\frac{f}{g}=\frac{a_{0}(\frac{p}{q}-\lambda_{1})\dots(\frac{p}{q}-\lambda_{m})}{b_{0}(\frac{p}{q}-\mu_{1})\dots(\frac{p}{q}-\mu_{l})}=\frac{a_{0}(p-\lambda_{1}q)\dots(p-\lambda_{m}q)q^{l-m}}{b_{0}(p-\mu_{1}q)\dots(p-\mu_{l}q)}.

and we obtain

b0​f​(p−μ1​q)​…​(p−μl​q)=a0​g​(p−λ1​q)​…​(p−λm​q)​ql−m.b_{0}f(p-\mu_{1}q)\dots(p-\mu_{l}q)=a_{0}g(p-\lambda_{1}q)\dots(p-\lambda_{m}q)q^{l-m}. (∗)

Note, as λi≠μj\lambda_{i}\neq\mu_{j}, the polynomials p−λi​qp-\lambda_{i}q and p−μj​qp-\mu_{j}q are coprime for all i=1,l¯i=\overline{1,l} and j=1,m¯j=\overline{1,m}. Moreover, since pp and qq are coprime, it is clear that qq is coprime with polynomials of the form p+α​qp+\alpha q, α∈𝕂\alpha\in\mathbb{K}.

Note also that p−β​q∉𝕂p-\beta q\not\in\mathbb{K}. Indeed, if p−β​q=ξ∈𝕂p-\beta q=\xi\in\mathbb{K} for some β,ξ∈𝕂\beta,\xi\in\mathbb{K}, then p=ξ+β​qp=\xi+\beta q and

φ=fg=a0​(ξ+(β−λ1)​q)​…​(ξ+(β−λm)​q)​ql−mb0​(ξ+(β−μ1​q)​…​(ξ+(β−μl)​q)CLOSE,\varphi=\frac{f}{g}=\frac{a_{0}(\xi+(\beta-\lambda_{1})q)\dots(\xi+(\beta-\lambda_{m})q)q^{l-m}}{b_{0}(\xi+(\beta-\mu_{1}q)\dots(\xi+(\beta-\mu_{l})q)},

which means that ff and gg are algebraically dependent, which contradicts our assumptions.

So from (∗)(*) we conclude that ff is divisible by all polynomials (p−λi​q)(p-\lambda_{i}q). Since ff is irreducible, taking into account the above considerations we conclude that m=1m=1 and f=a⁡(p−λ1​q)f=a(p-\lambda_{1}q), a∈𝕂∗a\in\mathbb{K}^{*}. Therefore, from (∗)(*) we obtain

b0​a​(p−λ1​q)​(p−μ1​q)​…​(p−μl​q)=a0​g​(p−λ1​q)​ql−1b_{0}a(p-\lambda_{1}q)(p-\mu_{1}q)\dots(p-\mu_{l}q)=a_{0}g(p-\lambda_{1}q)q^{l-1}

and after reduction

b0​a​(p−μ1​q)​…​(p−μl​q)=a0​g​ql−1.b_{0}a(p-\mu_{1}q)\dots(p-\mu_{l}q)=a_{0}gq^{l-1}.

Since qq is coprime with (p−μj​q)(p-\mu_{j}q), we get l=1l=1 and finally a0​g=b0​a​(p−μ1​q)a_{0}g=b_{0}a(p-\mu_{1}q). We obtain

φ=fg=a0​(p−λ1​q)b0​(p−μ1​q)=a0​(pq−λ1)b0​(pq−μ1)=a0​(ψ−λ1)b0​(ψ−μ1).\varphi=\frac{f}{g}=\frac{a_{0}(p-\lambda_{1}q)}{b_{0}(p-\mu_{1}q)}=\frac{a_{0}(\frac{p}{q}-\lambda_{1})}{b_{0}(\frac{p}{q}-\mu_{1})}=\frac{a_{0}(\psi-\lambda_{1})}{b_{0}(\psi-\mu_{1})}.

One concludes that 𝕂⁡(φ)=𝕂⁡(ψ)\mathbb{K}(\varphi)=\mathbb{K}(\psi), which means that φ\varphi is a closed rational function. ∎

3 Rational functions and pencils of hypersurfaces

In this section we give a characterization of closed rational functions. While proving Theorem  2 we use an approach from the paper of J.M.Ollagnier [Oll] connected with Darboux polynomials. Recall some notions and terminology (see also [Now1], pp.22-24). If δ\delta is a derivation of the polynomial ring 𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}], then a polynomial ff is called a Darboux polynomial for δ\delta if δ⁡(f)=λ​f\delta(f)=\lambda f for some polynomial λ\lambda (not necessarily λ∈𝕂\lambda\in\mathbb{K}). The polynomial λ\lambda is called the cofactor for δ\delta corresponding to the Darboux polynomial ff (so, ff is a polynomial eigenfunction for δ\delta and λ\lambda is the corresponding eigenvalue).

Further, for a rational function φ=fg∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\varphi=\frac{f}{g}\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} one can define a (vector) derivation δφ=g​d​f−f​d​g:𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]→Λ2​𝕂​[x1,…,xn]\delta_{\varphi}=gdf-fdg:\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}]\to\Lambda^{2}\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] by the rule δφ​(h)=d​h∧(g​d​f−f​d​g).\delta_{\varphi}(h)=dh\wedge(gdf-fdg). For such a derivation δφ\delta_{\varphi} a polynomial hh is called a Darboux polynomial if all coefficients of the 2−2-form d​h∧(g​d​f−f​d​g)dh\wedge(gdf-fdg) are divisible by the polynomial hh, i. e., d​h∧(g​d​f−f​d​g)=h⋅λdh\wedge(gdf-fdg)=h\cdot\lambda for some 2−2-form λ\lambda, which is called a cofactor for the derivation δφ.\delta_{\varphi}. Note that every divisor of the Darboux polynomial hh is also a Darboux polynomial for δφ\delta_{\varphi} (see, for example, [Now1], p.23). It is easy to see that the polynomial α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g is a Darboux polynomial for the derivation δφ\delta_{\varphi} and therefore every divisor of the polynomial α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g is a Darboux polynomial of the derivation δφ=g​d​f−f​d​g.\delta_{\varphi}=gdf-fdg.

Theorem 2.

Let polynomials f,g∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]f,g\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] be coprime and let at least one of them be a non-constant polynomial. Then the rational function φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} is closed if and only if all but finitely many hypersurfaces in the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g are irreducible.

Proof.

Let φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} be closed. Suppose that the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g contains infinitely many reducible hypersurfaces. Let {αi​f+βi​g}i∈ℕ\{\alpha_{i}f+\beta_{i}g\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}, (αi:βi)≠(αj:βj)(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})\neq(\alpha_{j}:\beta_{j}) for i≠ji\neq j as points of ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1}, be an infinite sequence of (different) reducible hypersurfaces. For each ii take one irreducible factor hih_{i} of αi​f+βi​g\alpha_{i}f+\beta_{i}g.

By the above remark, all polynomials hih_{i} are Darboux polynomials for δφ\delta_{\varphi} and deg⁡hi<deg⁡φ=:k\deg h_{i}<\deg\varphi=:k. By Corollary 5 from [Oll] there exist finitely many cofactors of δφ\delta_{\varphi} that correspond to Darboux polynomials hih_{i} (degrees of hih_{i} are bounded). Therefore, there exist polynomials hih_{i} and hjh_{j} such that δφ​(hi)=λ​hi\delta_{\varphi}(h_{i})=\lambda h_{i} and δφ​(hj)=λ​hj\delta_{\varphi}(h_{j})=\lambda h_{j} for some cofactor λ∈⋀2𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]\lambda\in\bigwedge^{2}\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}]. This implies δφ​(hihj)=0\delta_{\varphi}(\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}})=0 and thus d⁡(fg)∧d⁡(hihj)=1g2​δφ​(hihj)=0d(\frac{f}{g})\wedge d(\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}})=\frac{1}{g^{2}}\delta_{\varphi}(\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}})=0 (see [Oll]). By Lemma 2, the rational functions φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} and hihj\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}} are algebraically dependent. As φ\varphi is closed, hihj=F⁡(φ)\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}}=F(\varphi) for some F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t) and therefore deg⁡hihj=deg⁡F​deg⁡φ\deg\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}}=\deg F\deg\varphi (see for example [Oll]). But this is impossible since deg⁡hihj<deg⁡φ\deg\frac{h_{i}}{h_{j}}<\deg\varphi . Therefore, all but finitely many hypersurfaces in α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g are irreducible.

Let now α0​f+β0​g\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g be an irreducible hypersurface from the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g. Consider the case when ff and gg are algebraically independent. One can assume without loss of generality α0≠0\alpha_{0}\neq 0. Then α0​f+β0​g\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g and gg are algebraically independent as well. (If α0=0\alpha_{0}=0, then β0≠0\beta_{0}\neq 0 and polynomials ff and α0​f+β0​g\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g are algebraically independent). Therefore, since α0​f+β0​g\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g and gg are coprime, by Theorem 1 the rational function ψ=α0​f+β0​gg\psi=\frac{\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g}{g} is closed. Therefore, φ=fg=α0−1​(ψ−β0)\varphi=\frac{f}{g}=\alpha_{0}^{-1}(\psi-\beta_{0}), which proves that φ\varphi is a closed rational function.

Let now ff and gg be algebraically dependent. Then f=F⁡(h)f=F(h) and g=G⁡(h)g=G(h) for a common generative polynomial function hh and polynomials F⁡(t),G⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡[t]F(t),G(t)\in\mathbb{K}[t] (see Remark 2). Let (1:β1)≠(1:β2)(1:\beta_{1})\neq(1:\beta_{2}) be two different points in ℙ1\mathbb{P}^{1} such that f+βi​gf+\beta_{i}g is irreducible for i∈{1,2}i\in\{1,2\}. Then f+βi​g=F⁡(h)+βi​G​(h)f+\beta_{i}g=F(h)+\beta_{i}G(h) is irreducible for i∈{1,2}i\in\{1,2\}. In particular this means that deg⁡(F⁡(t)+βi​G​(t))=1\deg(F(t)+\beta_{i}G(t))=1, i. e., F⁡(t)+βi​G​(t)=ai​t+biF(t)+\beta_{i}G(t)=a_{i}t+b_{i}, ai,bi∈𝕂a_{i},b_{i}\in\mathbb{K}, ai≠0a_{i}\neq 0. Then since β1≠β2\beta_{1}\neq\beta_{2}, we conclude that F⁡(t)=a​t+bF(t)=at+b and G⁡(t)=c​t+dG(t)=ct+d for some a,b,c,d∈𝕂a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{K}. So φ=fg=a​h+bc​h+d\varphi=\frac{f}{g}=\frac{ah+b}{ch+d}. As at least one of ff and gg is non-constant and since ff and gg are coprime, we conclude that 𝕂⁡(φ)=𝕂⁡(h)\mathbb{K}(\varphi)=\mathbb{K}(h). Therefore, since 𝕂⁡(h)\mathbb{K}(h) is an algebraically closed subfield of the field 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}), φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} is a closed rational function. ∎

Remark 3.

Note, in order to show that φ=fg\varphi=\frac{f}{g} is closed in Theorem 2 it is enough to have two different irreducible hypersurfaces in the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g. One irreducible hypersurface α0​f+β0​g\alpha_{0}f+\beta_{0}g is enough provided ff and gg are algebraically independent.

Remark 4.

We also reproved a weak version (we do not give an estimation) of the next result of W.Ruppert (see [Rupp], Satz 6).

If ff and gg are algebraically independent polynomials and the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g contains at least one irreducible hypersurface, then all but finitely many hypersurfaces in α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g are irreducible.

Remark 5.

If a polynomial f∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]f\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] is non-constant then by Theorem 2 and Remark 2 ff is closed if and only if for all but finitely many λ∈𝕂\lambda\in\mathbb{K} the polynomial f+λf+\lambda is irreducible. This result is well-known (it can be proved by using the first Bertini theorem), see, for example, [Schinz], Corollary 3.3.1.

Using Remark 5 one can prove that any polynomial f∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]∖𝕂f\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}]\setminus\mathbb{K} can be written in the form f=F⁡(h)f=F(h) for some polynomial F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡[t]F(t)\in\mathbb{K}[t] and irreducible polynomial hh. Similar statement holds for rational functions.

Corollary 1.

A rational function fg∈𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)∖𝕂\frac{f}{g}\in\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n})\setminus\mathbb{K} can be written in the form fg=F⁡(φ)\frac{f}{g}=F(\varphi), F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t), for some rational function φ=pq\varphi=\frac{p}{q} such that polynomials pp and qq are irreducible.

Proof.

Let p1q1\frac{p_{1}}{q_{1}} be a generative function for fg\frac{f}{g}. As p1q1\frac{p_{1}}{q_{1}} is closed, by Theorem 2 the pencil α​p1+β​q1\alpha p_{1}+\beta q_{1} contains two different irreducible hypersurfaces p=α1​p1+β1​q1p=\alpha_{1}p_{1}+\beta_{1}q_{1} and q=α2​p1+β2​q1q=\alpha_{2}p_{1}+\beta_{2}q_{1}, i. e., (α1:β1)≠(α2:β2)(\alpha_{1}:\beta_{1})\neq(\alpha_{2}:\beta_{2}). Since the pencils α​p+β​q\alpha p+\beta q and α​p1+β​q1\alpha p_{1}+\beta q_{1} are equal, and since in the pencil α​p1+β​q1\alpha p_{1}+\beta q_{1} all but finitely many hypersurfaces are irreducible, we conclude that pq\frac{p}{q} is closed and is a generative function for fg\frac{f}{g}. ∎

Remark 6.

Under conditions of Corollary 1 polynomials pp and qq can be chosen of the same degree.

Corollary 2.

Let 𝕂⊆L⊆𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}\subseteq L\subseteq\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}) be an algebraically closed subfield in 𝕂⁡(x1,…,xn)\mathbb{K}(x_{1},\dots,x_{n}). Then it is possible to choose generators of LL in the form p1q1,…,pmqm\frac{p_{1}}{q_{1}},\dots,\frac{p_{m}}{q_{m}}, where pip_{i} and qiq_{i} are irreducible polynomials.

Theorem 3.

Let polynomials f,g∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]f,g\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] be coprime and algebraically independent. Then the rational function f/gf/g is not closed if and only if there exist algebraically independent irreducible polynomials pp and qq and a positive integer k⩾2k\geqslant 2 such that f=(α1​p+β1​q)​…​(αk​p+βk​q)f=(\alpha_{1}p+\beta_{1}q)\dots(\alpha_{k}p+\beta_{k}q) and g=(γ1​p+δ1​q)​…​(γk​p+δk​q)g=(\gamma_{1}p+\delta_{1}q)\dots(\gamma_{k}p+\delta_{k}q) for some (αi:βi),(γj:δj)∈ℙ1(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i}),(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j})\in\mathbb{P}_{1}, with (αi:βi)≠(γj:δj)(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})\neq(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j}), i,j=1,k¯i,j=\overline{1,k}.

Proof.

Suppose fg\frac{f}{g} is not closed. Take its generative function pq\frac{p}{q} with irreducible polynomials pp and qq. This is possible by Corollary 1. Then fg=F⁡(pq)\frac{f}{g}=F(\frac{p}{q}) for some rational function F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡(t)F(t)\in\mathbb{K}(t) with deg⁡F⁡(t)=k⩾2\deg F(t)=k\geqslant 2. Note that the polynomials pp and qq are algebraically independent because in other case the polynomials ff and gg were algebraically dependent which contradicts to our assumptions. Write

F⁡(t)=a0​(t−λ1)​…​(t−λs)b0​(t−μ1)​…​(t−μr)F(t)=\frac{a_{0}(t-\lambda_{1})\dots(t-\lambda_{s})}{b_{0}(t-\mu_{1})\dots(t-\mu_{r})}

with λi≠μj\lambda_{i}\neq\mu_{j}, i. e., with coprime nominator and denominator. It is clear that k=deg⁡F⁡(t)=max⁡{s,r}k=\deg F(t)=\max\{s,r\}. After substitution of tt by pq\frac{p}{q} we obtain

fg=a0​(p−λ1​q)​…​(p−λs​q)​qr−sb0​(p−μ1​q)​…​(p−μr​q).\frac{f}{g}=\frac{a_{0}(p-\lambda_{1}q)\dots(p-\lambda_{s}q)q^{r-s}}{b_{0}(p-\mu_{1}q)\dots(p-\mu_{r}q)}.

Put (αi:βi)=(1:−λi)(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})=(1:-\lambda_{i}) for i=1,s¯i=\overline{1,s}, (γj:δj)=(1:−μj)(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j})=(1:-\mu_{j}) for j=1,r¯j=\overline{1,r}. If r⩽sr\leqslant s, then put (γj:δj)=(0:1)(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j})=(0:1) for j=r+1,…,sj=r+1,\dots,s. If r>sr>s, then put (αi:βi)=(0:1)(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})=(0:1) for i=s+1,…,ri=s+1,\dots,r. We obtained

fg=a0​(α1​p+β1​q)​…​(αk​p+βk​q)b0​(γ1​p+δ1​q)​…​(γk​p+δk​q),\frac{f}{g}=\frac{a_{0}(\alpha_{1}p+\beta_{1}q)\dots(\alpha_{k}p+\beta_{k}q)}{b_{0}(\gamma_{1}p+\delta_{1}q)\dots(\gamma_{k}p+\delta_{k}q)},

which means that up to multiplication by a non-zero constant f=(α1​p+β1​q)​…​(αk​p+βk​q)f=(\alpha_{1}p+\beta_{1}q)\dots(\alpha_{k}p+\beta_{k}q) and g=(γ1​p+δ1​q)​…​(γk​p+δk​q)g=(\gamma_{1}p+\delta_{1}q)\dots(\gamma_{k}p+\delta_{k}q).

Suppose now that ff and gg have the form as in the conditions of this Theorem. Let us show that the rational function fg\frac{f}{g} is not closed. As f=(α1​p+β1​q)​…​(αk​p+βk​q)f=(\alpha_{1}p+\beta_{1}q)\dots(\alpha_{k}p+\beta_{k}q) and g=(γ1​p+δ1​q)​…​(γk​p+δk​q)g=(\gamma_{1}p+\delta_{1}q)\dots(\gamma_{k}p+\delta_{k}q), one has

fg=(α1​p+β1​q)​…​(αk​p+βk​q)(γ1​p+δ1​q)​…​(γk​p+δk​q)=(α1​pq+β1)​…​(αk​pq+βk)(γ1​pq+δ1)​…​(γk​pq+δk),\frac{f}{g}=\frac{(\alpha_{1}p+\beta_{1}q)\dots(\alpha_{k}p+\beta_{k}q)}{(\gamma_{1}p+\delta_{1}q)\dots(\gamma_{k}p+\delta_{k}q)}=\frac{(\alpha_{1}\frac{p}{q}+\beta_{1})\dots(\alpha_{k}\frac{p}{q}+\beta_{k})}{(\gamma_{1}\frac{p}{q}+\delta_{1})\dots(\gamma_{k}\frac{p}{q}+\delta_{k})},

i. e., fg=F⁡(pq)\frac{f}{g}=F(\frac{p}{q}) for the rational function F⁡(t)=(α1​t+β1)​…​(αk​t+βk)(γ1​t+δ1)​…​(γk​t+δk)F(t)=\frac{(\alpha_{1}t+\beta_{1})\dots(\alpha_{k}t+\beta_{k})}{(\gamma_{1}t+\delta_{1})\dots(\gamma_{k}t+\delta_{k})}. Since (αi:βi)≠(γj:δj)(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})\neq(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j}), i,j=1,k¯i,j=\overline{1,k}, we conclude that deg⁡F⁡(t)⩾2\deg F(t)\geqslant 2, which means that fg\frac{f}{g} is not closed (equivalently, by Theorem 2, the pencil α​f+β​g\alpha f+\beta g contains infinitely many reducible hypersurfaces). ∎

Example.

Let pp and qq be irreducible algebraically independent polynomials in 𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}], n⩾2n\geqslant 2. Then φ=plqm\varphi=\frac{p^{l}}{q^{m}} is a closed rational function for coprime ll and mm.

Indeed, suppose the converse holds. Then by Theorem 3 there exists irreducible polynomials p1p_{1} and q1q_{1}, an integer k⩾2k\geqslant 2 such that

plqm=(α1​p1+β1​q1)​…​(αk​p1+βk​q1)(γ1​p1+δ1​q1)​…​(γk​p1+δk​q1),(αi:βi)≠(γj:δj),i,j=1,k¯.\frac{p^{l}}{q^{m}}=\frac{(\alpha_{1}p_{1}+\beta_{1}q_{1})\dots(\alpha_{k}p_{1}+\beta_{k}q_{1})}{(\gamma_{1}p_{1}+\delta_{1}q_{1})\dots(\gamma_{k}p_{1}+\delta_{k}q_{1})},\quad(\alpha_{i}:\beta_{i})\neq(\gamma_{j}:\delta_{j}),\quad i,j=\overline{1,k}.

Since αi​p1+βi​q1\alpha_{i}p_{1}+\beta_{i}q_{1} and γj​p1+δj​q1\gamma_{j}p_{1}+\delta_{j}q_{1} are coprime for all ii and jj, it follows that pl=(α1​p1+β1​q1)​…​(αk​p1+βk​q1)p^{l}=(\alpha_{1}p_{1}+\beta_{1}q_{1})\dots(\alpha_{k}p_{1}+\beta_{k}q_{1}) and qm=(γ1​p1+δ1​q1)​…​(γk​p1+δk​q1)q^{m}=(\gamma_{1}p_{1}+\delta_{1}q_{1})\dots(\gamma_{k}p_{1}+\delta_{k}q_{1}). Since pp and qq are algebraically independent, as in the proof of Theorem 1 we conclude that α​p1+β​q1≠𝕂\alpha p_{1}+\beta q_{1}\neq\mathbb{K} for all (α:β)∈ℙ1(\alpha:\beta)\in\mathbb{P}^{1}. Therefore, (α1:β1)=⋯=(αk:βk),(\alpha_{1}:\beta_{1})=\dots=(\alpha_{k}:\beta_{k}), (γ1:δ1)=⋯=(γk:δk),(\gamma_{1}:\delta_{1})=\dots=(\gamma_{k}:\delta_{k}), and

pl=a0​(α1​p1+β1​q1)k,qm=b0​(γ1​p1+δ1​q1)k.p^{l}=a_{0}(\alpha_{1}p_{1}+\beta_{1}q_{1})^{k},\quad q^{m}=b_{0}(\gamma_{1}p_{1}+\delta_{1}q_{1})^{k}.

Since pp and qq are irreducible, we obtain, up to multiplication by a non-zero constant, α1​p1+β1​q1=pl′\alpha_{1}p_{1}+\beta_{1}q_{1}=p^{l^{\prime}} and γ1​p1+δ1​q1=qm′\gamma_{1}p_{1}+\delta_{1}q_{1}=q^{m^{\prime}}, i. e., k⩾2k\geqslant 2 divides both ll and mm. This is impossible, since ll and mm are coprime. We obtained a contradiction, which proves that plqm\frac{p^{l}}{q^{m}} is a closed rational function.

4 Products of irreducible polynomials

Theorem 4.

Let p1,…,pk∈𝕂⁡[x1,…,xn]p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\in\mathbb{K}[x_{1},\dots,x_{n}] be irreducible algebraically independent polynomials. If gcd⁡(m1,m2,…​mk)=1\gcd(m_{1},m_{2},\ldots m_{k})=1 then the polynomial

p1m1​p2m2​…​pkmk+λp_{1}^{m_{1}}p_{2}^{m_{2}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}}+\lambda

is irreducible for all but finitely many λ∈𝕂\lambda\in\mathbb{K}.

Proof.

Show at first that the polynomial p1m1​p2m2​…​pkmkp_{1}^{m_{1}}p_{2}^{m_{2}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}} is closed. Suppose to the contrary it is not closed and let p1m1​p2m2​…​pkmk=F⁡(h)p_{1}^{m_{1}}p_{2}^{m_{2}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}}=F(h) for some closed polynomial hh and F⁡(t)∈𝕂⁡[t]F(t)\in\mathbb{K}[t], deg⁡F⁡(t)⩾2\deg F(t)\geqslant 2. Let F⁡(t)=α⁡(t−μ1)​…​(t−μs)F(t)=\alpha(t-\mu_{1})\dots(t-\mu_{s}) be the decomposition of F⁡(t)F(t) into linear factors. Then

p1m1​p2m2​…​pkmk=α⁡(h−μ1)​…​(h−μs),μ∈𝕂,α∈𝕂∗.p_{1}^{m_{1}}p_{2}^{m_{2}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}}=\alpha(h-\mu_{1})\dots(h-\mu_{s}),\quad\mu\in\mathbb{K},\quad\alpha\in\mathbb{K}^{*}.

Since the polynomials h−μih-\mu_{i} are closed and since we assumed that the polynomial p1m1​p2m2​…​pkmkp_{1}^{m_{1}}p_{2}^{m_{2}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}} is not closed, one concludes that s⩾2s\geqslant 2. Suppose there exists μi≠μj\mu_{i}\neq\mu_{j}, assume without loss of generality μ1≠μ2\mu_{1}\neq\mu_{2}. As all pip_{i} are irreducible, it is clear that h−μ1=α1​pi1s1​…​pimsmh-\mu_{1}=\alpha_{1}p_{i_{1}}^{s_{1}}\dots p_{i_{m}}^{s_{m}} and h−μ2=α2​pj1t1​…​pjrtrh-\mu_{2}=\alpha_{2}p_{j_{1}}^{t_{1}}\dots p_{j_{r}}^{t_{r}} for pi1,…,pim,pj1,…,pjr∈{p1,…,pk}p_{i_{1}},\dots,p_{i_{m}},p_{j_{1}},\dots,p_{j_{r}}\in\{p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\}. Since μ1≠μ2\mu_{1}\neq\mu_{2}, the polynomials h−μ1h-\mu_{1} and h−μ2h-\mu_{2} are coprime. Therefore, the sets {pi1,…,pim}\{p_{i_{1}},\dots,p_{i_{m}}\} and {pj1,…,pjr}\{p_{j_{1}},\dots,p_{j_{r}}\} are disjoint. From (h−μ1)−(h−μ2)+(μ1−μ2)=0(h-\mu_{1})-(h-\mu_{2})+(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2})=0 it follows that

α1​pi1s1​…​pimsm−α2​pj1t1​…​pjrtr+(μ1−μ2)=0,\alpha_{1}p_{i_{1}}^{s_{1}}\dots p_{i_{m}}^{s_{m}}-\alpha_{2}p_{j_{1}}^{t_{1}}\dots p_{j_{r}}^{t_{r}}+(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2})=0,

which means that the set {p1,…,pk}\{p_{1},\dots,p_{k}\} is algebraically dependent. We obtained a contradiction. Therefore, μ1=⋯=μs\mu_{1}=\dots=\mu_{s} and p1m1​…​pkmk=α​(h−μ1)sp_{1}^{m_{1}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}}=\alpha(h-\mu_{1})^{s}, s⩾2s\geqslant 2. From the unique factorization of the polynomial p1m1​…​pkmkp_{1}^{m_{1}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}} it follows that s|m1,…,s|mks|m_{1},\ldots,s|m_{k} which is impossible by our restriction on numbers m1,…,mk.m_{1},\ldots,m_{k}. This contradiction proves that the polynomial p1m1​…​pkmkp_{1}^{m_{1}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}} is closed. Therefore, by Remark 5 the polynomial p1m1​…​pkmk+λp_{1}^{m_{1}}\dots p_{k}^{m_{k}}+\lambda is irreducible for all but finitely many λ∈𝕂\lambda\in\mathbb{K}.

∎
